name: Ubuntu (Relational Ethics)
summary: Ethical framework rooted in communal personhood — 'I am because we are' — encoding mutual obligation, restorative justice, and collective dignity.

claims.statement: Ubuntu ethics provided the philosophical basis for South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission
Relational personhood concepts appear independently across Bantu-speaking societies and beyond

evidence.source: Metz (2007) Toward an African Moral Theory, Journal of Political Philosophy
Proverbs and oral traditions across Zulu, Xhosa, Shona, and Sotho cultures

notes: Not merely a philosophy but an active social technology — shapes conflict resolution, resource sharing, and identity formation.
